title: Velocity Platform — Procurement acceptance and keying walkthrough
summary: High-level procurement/technical sync to align on MSA/DPA redlines, KMS & SSO requirements, pricing band for reserved capacity, and onboarding timeline. Customer asked for explicit egress accounting and private VPC deployment option with customer-managed keys. Action items and pilot dates agreed.
topics: SLA tiers and SSO / SAML integration
transcript:
Meeting header: Recorded 2026-06-05 15:30 UTC | Duration 47m | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Jordan (Redwood) + Aisha, Marco, Priya, Samir, Evan (Velocity)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, say your name and role.
[00:07] Aisha Khan: Aisha, procurement. Hi.
[00:09] Marco Diaz: Marco, legal.
[00:11] Priya Reddy: Priya, head of platform.
[00:13] Samir Patel: Samir, DevOps.
[00:15] Evan Lee: Evan, finance.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great. Liam and I from Redwood — Liam is our solutions engineer; Jordan's here for onboarding / support.
[00:26] Liam O'Connor: Hi all.

[02:05] Maya Chen: Agenda is procurement acceptance, keying walk — high level — and then technical clarifs. We want to make sure legal and procurement have what you need to complete vendor approval.
[02:20] Aisha Khan: Yes, the procurement team wants the scope of the DPA exceptions up front; any data residency notes, and the SLA thresholds that map to our ops acceptance criteria.
[02:33] Marco Diaz: And I'd like to walk through the MSA redlines we circulated. There are three points: indemnity, data return/deletion timing, and privileged keying.

[04:10] Liam O'Connor: On the technical side, we support three deployment modes — hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For Velocity's regulated workloads we recommended Private with customer-managed KMS.
[04:40] Priya Reddy: Can you clarify "customer-managed KMS"? We need to know if Redwood ever sees plaintext keys or if the HSM stays under our control.
[04:52] Liam O'Connor: Short answer: with our Private offering you can bring your own KMS via standard cloud KMS integrations (we support AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault) or HSMs via bring-your-own-key flows. We never store unwrapped customer model keys in our control plane. There are caveats for on-prem package where physical key custody depends on the deployment architecture.
[05:20] Samir Patel: So who rotates keys and who can decrypt logs?
[05:26] Liam O'Connor: Key rotation is customer-driven for BYOK. Logs that contain encrypted artifacts will remain encrypted; we do keep service-level logs for telemetry but they won't contain plaintext PII or customer keys. We can provide a log redaction spec.

[07:05] Marco Diaz: On the MSA indemnity, there's language about third-party claims tied to model outputs. We're asking for a carve-out for regulated domain-specific outputs — basically we need a mutual limitation for claims that arise from customer-supplied data and prompts.
[07:32] Maya Chen: Understood. We can map that to the standard carve used in enterprise MSA: obligation for the customer to provide prompt context and to run the evals. Redwood's liability centers on platform security and gross negligence. I'll escalate to legal for a tracked redline we can sign off.

[09:00] Evan Lee: Pricing — we need an estimate for committed reserved capacity for 2-year term. Also, can you give an egress estimate? Our finance team hates surprise bandwidth charges.
[09:18] Jordan Park: For 2-year reserved pools we offer tiered discounts based on committed GPU hours and model families. Egress is billed as outbound data transfer — we can provide an SKU-level estimate if you share expected tokens per month and embedding volumes. We can also propose a blended price for a pilot to avoid variable egress during initial months.
[09:45] Priya Reddy: We'll send a short workbook with traffic profile, yes.

[11:10] Aisha Khan: Procurement needs to confirm data residency and SOC 2 attestation dates. We also need the DPA with data sub-processing and any subprocessor list.
[11:22] Maya Chen: We publish SOC 2 Type II report; current date is May 2026 — we'll share the letter and a list of subprocessors. For Private deployments, subprocessors are limited as most infra stays customer-side. DPA — we can reuse our standard DPA but we'll flag any subprocessor items and customs.

[13:05] Samir Patel: Regarding network and egress — if we run Private in our VPC, does traffic ever route through Redwood control plane in plaintext?
[13:18] Liam O'Connor: For VPC private we offer a customer-facing control plane that can be on your network — flows are configurable. We support mTLS and PrivateLink-style endpoints. Nothing should egress through Redwood's public network unless you choose hosted fallback. We'll document the network topology.

[15:00] Marco Diaz: Back to keying — we have requirement for key escrow and rotation audit logs. Can Redwood provide HSM-backed signing and audit trails accessible to our auditors?
[15:18] Jordan Park: We can expose audit logs via secure log push to your SIEM or S3 with encryption. For HSM-backed signing we can integrate with your HSM for key ops; for hosted we rely on cloud KMS but can prove KMS operations via CloudTrail-like logs. We'll include an example schema.

[17:30] Priya Reddy: Performance question — our ML team wants guarantees on latency for 512-token completion and large embedding bulk jobs. What SLA tiers map to that?
[17:44] Liam O'Connor: SLA tiers are tied to deployment mode and commitment. Dedicated pools have p99 latency SLOs across certain model families. We can provide model-specific perf profiles. For strict p99 sub-second it's usually on smaller models or highly provisioned pools. We'll send the performance profile table.

[19:20] Aisha Khan: Procurement asks could you insert a clause limiting price increases within renewal windows? We need predictability.
[19:30] Maya Chen: We understand; standard enterprise contracts include CPI-based caps or fixed rate schedules for renewals. We'll propose a renewal pricing table and commit to 90-day advance notice for material pricing changes.

[21:05] Marco Diaz: On DPA deletion requests — our policy is 30 days for deletion of customer data for production datasets. Your DPA currently lists 60 days. Can that be shortened?
[21:20] Maya Chen: We can discuss 30-day deletion for data at rest in hosted instances, subject to subprocessor timelines. For cached KV/prefix caches there may be replication timing — we can commit to a best-effort 30 days and a contractual note for any edge caches. I'll mark that as a DPA redline to target.

[23:40] Evan Lee: Pilot timeline — we want a two-week smoke test, then a 6-week pilot. What resource commitment do you need from Redwood?
[23:55] Jordan Park: For the pilot we recommend an onboarding engineer (2 days), an SE-run benchmark of your prompt set and some reserved capacity for deterministic results. We'll provide scripts and a perf spreadsheet. Expect a 1-week setup, 2-week smoke, and then 4-week pilot for feature validation.

[26:10] Samir Patel: For access control — we need SSO with SCIM provisioning and role-based access control so engineers can't request keys.
[26:21] Liam O'Connor: We support SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is configurable at team and API key level. We'll send the SCIM mapping doc.

[28:12] Priya Reddy: Are there any export controls or restrictions on model families we should worry about?
[28:22] Maya Chen: Some model families have geo restrictions; we'll flag models with export constraints. For on-prem you control the model weights entirely.

[30:05] Marco Diaz: Another legal nit — we want a clause that requires Redwood to notify us within 72 hours of a security incident affecting our data. Your MSA says "reasonable" timeframe. Can we make that explicit?
[30:18] Maya Chen: Yes, 72 hours is reasonable for incident notification. We'll propose a redline to replace "reasonable" with "within 72 hours of detection" and include a post-incident report timeline.

[33:00] Aisha Khan: Procurement also needs an SLA credit matrix if p99 latency or availability is missed.
[33:12] Jordan Park: We have standard credit tiers for availability and SLO misses by deployment. For Dedicated we'll present a table with percentage credits tied to monthly availability bands. We'll attach the credit table to the SOW.

[35:40] Priya Reddy: Onboarding checklist — can you summarize what we own vs Redwood owns?
[35:48] Maya Chen: Sure: Velocity owns VPC, KMS, identity provider, ingress ACLs, and prompt/data governance; Redwood owns runtime, model packaging, serving runtime, observability agents, and the onboarding engineer support. We'll send a one-pager ownership matrix.

[38:10] Samir Patel: Regarding backups — how are models and logs backed up and what's retention?
[38:19] Liam O'Connor: Backups are config/metadata and model weights snapshots; retention is configurable and we can match your retention policy. Logs retention is per plan; for long-term retention we offer an archive export to your storage.

[40:00] Marco Diaz: Could you provide a redline-ready MSA with the proposed edits so legal can mark up rather than starting from blank?
[40:09] Maya Chen: Absolutely — next steps we'll send a redline with the 72-hour incident clause, 30-day deletion target, BYOK escape clause, and renewal price protection.

[42:45] Evan Lee: Finance wants the workbook and rough committed pricing by next Tuesday. Is that doable?
[42:52] Jordan Park: Yes — if you send the workbook today we'll return a draft committed quote by next Tuesday.

[44:10] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send — (1) redline MSA+DPA with noted items, (2) SOC2 letter and subprocessor list, (3) SCIM mapping and KMS audit schema, (4) pilot SOW and perf spreadsheet, (5) draft committed pricing. Velocity to send traffic workbook and any final legal priority list.
[44:38] Priya Reddy: We'll send the prompt/traffic workbook by end of day Friday.
[44:45] Aisha Khan: Procurement will review redline and aim for internal approval window after you send the documents.

[46:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to docs. Meeting adjourned.

[46:30] (recording ends)
next_steps: Redwood: send redline MSA+DPA (includes 72-hour incident clause)
Redwood: share SOC2 report and subprocessors list
Redwood: send SCIM mapping and KMS audit schema
Redwood: deliver pilot SOW and perf spreadsheet
Velocity: send traffic & prompt workbook by 2026-06-11

Jordan Park: produce pilot SOW and perf scripts (due 2026-06-08)
Jordan Park: draft committed pricing based on workbook (due 2026-06-09)
